# NcPasswords

> NcPasswords is a free, open-source (MIT) Windows 10/11 desktop app for the Nextcloud Passwords app. You sign in once with your Nextcloud server address, username and password (or an app password with two-factor authentication), and can then browse, search and copy your saved logins from the desktop without opening a browser. Everything it stores is encrypted on the local PC.

Key facts:

- Current version: 0.2.0. Platform: Windows 10 and 11 (x64). Distributed as an installer (per-user, no administrator rights) and as a portable ZIP.
- It talks only to the Nextcloud server the user enters. No analytics, no relay, no other backend.
- The Nextcloud login and the cached entries are encrypted with Windows DPAPI (per user). An optional additional local password, set at sign-in, is required on every start; it is never written to disk, only a salt used to derive a key from it.
- Entries are cached locally, so the app works offline and refreshes when opened.
- Folders and entries are shown in one combined tree, modeled after Password Safe. Each entry shows its name and username; details (URL, notes, tags, custom fields) open in a details view.
- Double-click copies the password, Ctrl+C copies the username; the clipboard is cleared after 30 seconds. Search filters by name, username, URL and notes as you type.
- Closing the window keeps it running in the system tray.
- Not supported: accounts with Nextcloud Passwords client-side encryption enabled (the app shows a message).
- The app is not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen shows an "unknown publisher" warning on first run ("More info" → "Run anyway").
- It is an independent project, not affiliated with Nextcloud GmbH, built with help from Claude, and has not had a third-party security audit.

- [Nextcloud Passwords](https://apps.nextcloud.com/apps/passwords): the Nextcloud server app NcPasswords connects to
- [Password Safe](https://github.com/pwsafe/pwsafe): the desktop password manager whose layout NcPasswords follows
